Chronotope.fact: In literary theory and philosophy of language, the chronotope is how configurations of time and space are represented in language and discourse. The term itself comes from the Russian xронотоп, which in turn is derived from the Greek χρόνος ('time') and τόπος ('space'); it thus can be literally translated as "time-space."
